# Quantitative partial regularity of the Navier-Stokes equations and applications

Zhen Lei $^{*}$

Xiao Ren $^{\dagger}$

October 5, 2022

## Abstract

We prove a logarithmic improvement of the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg partial regularity theorem for the Navier-Stokes equations. The key idea is to find a quantitative counterpart for the absolute continuity of the dissipation energy using the pigeonhole principle. Based on the same method, for any suitable weak solution, we show the existence of intervals of regularity in one spatial direction with length depending exponentially on the natural local energies of the solution. Then, we give two applications of the latter result in the axially symmetric case. The first one is a local quantitative regularity criterion for suitable weak solutions with small swirl. The second one is a slightly improved one-point CKN criterion which implies all known (slightly supercritical) Type I regularity results in the literature.

## 1 Introduction

We study the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in three dimensions:

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{c} \partial_ {t} v - \Delta v + (v \cdot \nabla) v + \nabla p = 0, \\ \nabla \cdot v = 0, \end{array} \right.
$$

(NS)

where $v,p$ are the unknown velocity and pressure fields. Whether the solutions to (NS) can develop finite time singularities from regular initial data remains a question of central importance in the theory of partial differential equations. It has been called one of the seven most important unsolved problems by the Clay Mathematics Institute, see [11].

In 1934, based on the natural energy structure of (NS), Leray [19] constructed global weak solutions for the Cauchy problem of (NS) with finite kinetic energy $\sup_{t\geq 0}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{3}}|v|^{2}dx$ and finite dissipation energy (Dirichlet integral) $\int_{0}^{+\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{3}}|\nabla v|^{2}dxdt.$ Moreover, for these solutions the global energy inequality

$$
\int_ {\mathbb {R} ^ {3} \times \{t \}} | v | ^ {2} d x + 2 \int_ {0} ^ {t} \int_ {\mathbb {R} ^ {3}} | \nabla v | ^ {2} d x d t \leq \int_ {\mathbb {R} ^ {3} \times \{0 \}} | v | ^ {2} d x
$$

(1.1)

holds for a.a. $t > 0$ . Later, Hopf [12] obtained a similar existence result for the boundary value problem of (NS) on bounded domains. As well-known, (NS) enjoys a natural scaling invariance property, namely, for any solution $(v,p)$ to (NS), the rescaled functions

$$
v ^ {(\lambda)} (x, t) = \lambda v (\lambda x, \lambda^ {2} t), p ^ {(\lambda)} (x, t) = \lambda^ {2} p (\lambda x, \lambda^ {2} t)
$$

(1.2)

also satisfy (NS) for any $\lambda>0$ . The kinetic and dissipation energies of (NS) are both supercritical with respect to the natural scaling of (NS), namely, the energies of the zoomed-in solution $v^{(\lambda)}$ with $\lambda<1$ are greater than those of the original solution v. This indicates that the a priori estimates of the Leray-Hopf weak solutions are too weak to control the behavior of v on fine scales.

In the papers [27, 28], Scheffer initiated the study of partial regularity for the Navier-Stokes equations, that is, to estimate the dimension of the potential singular set of a weak solution. He considered a subclass of the Leray-Hopf weak solutions satisfying the local energy inequality, and proved that the singular set is of Hausdorff dimension no more than $\frac{5}{3}$ . In the landmark work of Caffarelli, Kohn and Nirenberg [3], Scheffer's result is improved, and it is shown that the 1d parabolic Hausdorff measure of the singular set is equal to 0 for a class of suitable weak solutions. [3] is a foundation for many important results later, e.g., the $L_{t}^{\infty}L_{x}^{3}$ regularity criterion [9], backward and forward self-similar solutions [26, 14], regularity via Liouville theorems [16], etc. Simplified proofs of the partial regularity theorem are given by Lin [20], Ladyzhenskaya-Seregin [17] and Vasseur [35]. To describe the theory precisely, we recall a few important notions.

Definition 1. We say that a point $w=(x,t)$ is a regular point of $v$ , if $v$ is bounded (and Hölder continuous) in $Q(r,w)$ for some $r>0$ . Here $Q(r,w)=Q(r)+w$ and $Q(r)=B(r)\times(-r^{2},0)$ . We say that $w$ is a singular point of $v$ if it is not regular. We denote the singular set of $v$ by $\mathcal{S}[v]$ . For a solution $v$ in the spacetime cylinder $Q(1)$ , it is understood that $\mathcal{S}[v]\subset Q(1)\cup(B(1)\times\{0\})$ .

Definition 2. We say that a pair of functions $(v,p)$ is a local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations in the domain $\mathcal{D}\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ , if the following conditions hold.

$$
1. v \in L _ {t} ^ {\infty} L _ {x} ^ {2} (\mathcal {D}), \nabla v \in L _ {t} ^ {2} L _ {x} ^ {2} (\mathcal {D}), p \in L _ {t} ^ {\frac {3}{2}} L _ {x} ^ {\frac {3}{2}} (\mathcal {D}).
$$

2. $v,p$ satisfy the Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathcal{D}$ in the sense of distributions.

3. v,p satisfy the local energy inequality

2. $v,p$ satisfy the Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathcal{D}$ in the sense of distributions.

3. v,p satisfy the local energy inequality

$$
\begin{array}{l} \int_ {\mathcal {D} _ {T}} | v | ^ {2} \phi d x + 2 \int_ {- \infty} ^ {T} \int_ {\mathcal {D} _ {t}} | \nabla v | ^ {2} \phi d x d t \leq \\ \leq \int_ {- \infty} ^ {T} \int_ {\mathcal {D} _ {t}} \left[ | v | ^ {2} \left(\phi_ {t} + \Delta \phi\right) + (| v | ^ {2} + 2 p) v \cdot \nabla \phi \right] d x d t. \\ \end{array}
$$

(1.3)

for any nonnegative function $\phi\in C_{0}^{\infty}(\mathcal{D})$ . Here, $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ is the time t slice of $\mathcal{D},$ i.e., $\mathcal{D}_{t}=\mathcal{D}\cap(\mathbb{R}^{3}\times\{t\})$ .

(Note that this is the definition from [20], and the assumption on pressure is stronger than that in [3].)

Although it is not clear whether all Leray-Hopf weak solutions are suitable, in the appendix of [3] the authors were able to construct suitable Leray-Hopf weak solutions for the Cauchy problem and the boundary value problem of (NS) with general $L^{2}$ initial data. See also [20, Lemma 2.3] or [17, Theorem 1.1] for the a priori estimates on the pressure.

Definition 3. For any non-negative function $f(r)$ defined on some interval $[0,\delta_{0})_{r}$ with $f(0)=0$ , we define the parabolic f-Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ as

$$
\mathcal {P} ^ {f} (\mathcal {S}) = \lim _ {\delta \rightarrow 0 +} \mathcal {P} _ {\delta} ^ {f} (\mathcal {S})
$$

(1.4)

with

$$
\mathcal {P} _ {\delta} ^ {f} (\mathcal {S}) = \inf \left\{\sum_ {i = 1} ^ {+ \infty} f \left(r _ {i}\right): \left\{Q \left(r _ {i}, w _ {i}\right) \right\} _ {i = 1} ^ {+ \infty} \text {is a c o v e r i n g o f} \mathcal {S}, 0 \leq r _ {i} \leq \delta \right\}
$$

(1.5)

where $Q ( r_{i}, w_{i} )=B ( r_{i}) \times(-r_{i}^{2}, 0)+w_{i}$ $\mathcal{P}^{f}$ is a special case of Caratheodory's construction, see [10, Section 2.10]. For $f ( r )=r^{\alpha}$ , this is the parabolic $\alpha$ -dimensional Hausdorff measure introduced in [3], and we simply write $\mathcal{P}^{f}=\mathcal{P}^{\alpha}$

The classical partial regularity theorem of Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg reads

Theorem 4 (CKN partial regularity). For a local suitable weak solutuion $(v,p)$ to the Navier-Stokes equations, $\mathcal{P}^{1}(\mathcal{S}[v])=0.$

The proof of Theorem 4 is based on the important $\varepsilon$ -regularity criterion. Using the a priori bounds in Definition 2 and interpolation, we know that $v \in L_{t}^{s}L_{x}^{l}(Q(1))$ for any s, l satisfying $\frac{2}{s}+\frac{3}{l}=\frac{3}{2},$ l $\in[2,6].$ We define the functionals

(1.6)

$$
\mathcal {G} = \mathcal {G} [ v, p ] \triangleq \int_ {Q (1)} \left(| v | ^ {3} + | p | ^ {3 / 2}\right) d x d t < + \infty
$$

$$
\mathcal {H} = \mathcal {H} [ v ] \triangleq \int_ {Q (1)} | \nabla v | ^ {2} d x d t < + \infty
$$

and

(1.7)

for a suitable weak solution $( v,p)$ . By (1.3), the kinetic and the dissipation energies of v on $Q(r)$ for any $r < 1$ are bounded in terms of $\mathcal{G}[v,p]$

Theorem 5 (local $\varepsilon$ - regularity). Let $v$ be a local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations in Q(1), there exists an absolute positive constant $\varepsilon_{*}$ such that if

$$
\mathcal {G} [ v, p ] \leq \varepsilon_ {*},
$$

(1.8)

then $v$ is Hölder continuous in $Q\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, and satisfies the pointwise estimates

$$
\left\| \nabla_ {x} ^ {m} v \right\| _ {L ^ {\infty} (Q (1 / 2))} \lesssim_ {m} 1, \quad m = 0, 1, 2, \dots .
$$

(1.9)

We refer to [3, 20, 17, 35] for proofs of the Hölder continuity of v in Theorem 5, and to [22, Proposition 2.1] for a remark on how to obtain the higher regularity estimates. Note that the methods in [20, 17] rely on certain (non-quantitative) compactness arguments, while the method in [35] based on the De Giorgi iteration is quantitative. With the help of Theorem 5 and an iteration of scale-invariant quantities, the one-point regularity criterion Theorem 6 can be established. Then, Theorem 4 is a corollary of Theorem 6 and the absolute continuity of the dissipation energy $\int |\nabla v|^{2} d x d t.$

Theorem 6 (CKN criterion). Let v be a local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations in Q(1). There exists a universal positive constant $\varepsilon_{**}$ such that

Theorem 6 (CKN criterion). Let v be a local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations in Q(1). There exists a universal positive constant $\varepsilon_{**}$ such that

$$
\limsup _ {r \rightarrow 0 +} \frac {1}{r} \int_ {Q (r)} | \nabla v | ^ {2} d x d t \leq \varepsilon_ {* *} \Longrightarrow (0, 0) \notin \mathcal {S} [ v ].
$$

(1.10)

We point out that the proof of Theorem 4 in [3] is still non-quantitative, essentially because the absolute continuity of the dissipation energy is a non-quantitative fact. Given any integrable function $g$ on $Q(1)$, it is well-known that for any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $\int_{U}|g|dxdt < \varepsilon$ for any $U$ with $|U| \triangleq \int_{U}1dxdt < \delta$. However, it is

clearly impossible to give an explicit dependence of $\delta$ on $\epsilon$ unless higher integrability of g is assumed.

Remarkably, Choe and Lewis [8] improved Theorem 4 for the first time and showed that $\mathcal{P}^{f}(\mathcal{S}[v])=0$ for $f(r)=r|\ln r|^{\alpha}$ for a small positive $\alpha$ (precisely $0\leq\alpha<\frac{3}{44}$ ). The key step is to show that $\ln(1/d)|\nabla v|^{2}$ is locally integrable where d is the parabolic distance to certain subsets of the singular set. See also the work [25] for an improvement on the range of $\alpha.$

For any singular point $w=(x,t)\in S[v]$ , we say that w is Type I if

$$
\limsup _ {r \rightarrow 0 +} \frac {1}{r} \int_ {Q (r, w)} | \nabla v | ^ {2} d x d t < + \infty .
$$

(1.11)

For $w=(0, 0)$ , the pointwise upper bound

(1.12)

$$
| v | \leq \frac {C _ {*}}{\sqrt {| x | ^ {2} - t}}, \mathrm {f o r} (x, t) \in Q (r), r > 0
$$

would imply (1.11). It is a major open problem in the field to rule out the possibility of blow-up under the condition (1.11) or (1.12). In other words, it is of great importance to improve the CKN criterion Theorem 6, in particular, to remove the smallness requirement there.

## 1.1 Main results

## 1.1.1 Quantitative partial regularity

In this paper, we first give a further improvement on the partial regularity theorem using a different approach from [8].

Theorem A (Improved partial regularity). Let $v$ be a local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equation in $Q(1)$, then we have, for $f(r) = r|\ln r|$,

Theorem A (Improved partial regularity). Let $v$ be a local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equation in $Q(1)$, then we have, for $f(r) = r|\ln r|$,

$$
\mathcal {P} ^ {f} \left(\mathcal {S} [ v ]\right) = 0.
$$

(1.13)

Remark 7. This result remains true for the forced Navier-Stokes equations with external force g belonging to $L_{x,t}^{q},$ q> $\frac{5}{2}$ . Such an external force term can be treated by introducing $r^{3 q-5}\int_{Q(r)}|g|^{q}dxdt$ in the iteration of scale-invariant quantities and applying the forced $\varepsilon$ - regularity criterion, see [3, Corollary 1]. Moreover, in (1.13) we can even take $f(r)=r|\ln r| \cdot\ln\ln|\ln r|.$ Since those bring no additional difficulty in our analysis, we shall focus on the unforced equation and the particular choice of f in this article.

The key idea is to find a sharp quantitative counterpart for the absolute continuity property of the dissipation energy $\int |\nabla v|^{2} d x d t.$ For any integrable function g defined on an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and any sequence of open sets $U_{k}\subset\Omega,$ consider the quantities

$$
\mathcal {E} _ {k} = \int_ {U _ {k} \backslash U _ {k + 1}} | g | d x.
$$

(1.14)

$\mathcal{E}_{k}$ satisfies the non-overlapping property

$$
\sum_ {k \geq 1} \mathcal {E} _ {k} \leq \int_ {\Omega} | g | d x,
$$

(1.15)

$\mathcal{E}_{k}$ satisfies the non-overlapping property

$$
\sum_ {k \geq 1} \mathcal {E} _ {k} \leq \int_ {\Omega} | g | d x,
$$

(1.15)

which enables the application of the pigeonhole principle. In particular, we have a sequence of $k_{j}\rightarrow+\infty$ such that $\mathcal{E}_{k_{j}}\leq o(\frac{1}{k_{j}\ln k_{j}}).$ We will take $g=|\nabla v|^{2}$ , and this

observation provides a crucial extra smallness leading to the improvement of partial regularity.

Another ingredient in the proof of Theorem A is to obtain an iteration of the scale-invariant quantities $A(r), E(r), F(r)$ and $D(r)$ (see Section 2.1) based on the energy structure of the Navier-Stokes equations, assuming the smallness of $\widetilde{E}(r)= r^{-\frac{14}{9}}\left(\int_{Q(r)}|\nabla v|^{\frac{9}{5}}dxdt\right)^{\frac{10}{9}}$ instead of $E(r)=\frac{1}{r}\int_{Q(r)}|\nabla v|^{2}dxdt$ (see Lemmas 10, 11 and 15 for details). Note that the quantity $\widetilde{E}$ was already used by Choe and Lewis in [8]. The main novelty here is the iteration argument.

Next, we turn to our second main result concerning quantitative intervals of regularity. It is well-known that one cannot expect regularity estimates only in terms of the local kinetic and dissipation energies due to the supercritical nature of the Navier-Stokes equations. In the next result, based on the quantitative method described above, we show that such regularity estimates are nevertheless valid in certain intervals of regularity for any local suitable weak solution. Let v be a local suitable weak solution in $Q(1)$ and $\pi_{3}$ be the projection map to the $x_{3}$ -axis. According to Theorem 4, the 1D Hausdorff measure of $\pi_{3} ( S[v] )=\{-1<z<1: \mathbb{R}^{2}\times\{z\} \times\mathbb{R}\cap S[v]\neq\emptyset\}$ must be zero. Note that $\pi_{3} ( S[v]\cap Q(\rho) )$ is a closed set for any $\rho<1.$ Hence, for any open interval $( a,b)\subset(-1,1),$ there exists a subinterval $( z_{1},z_{2} )\subset(a,b)$ such that v is regular in the strip $\{(x,t)\in Q(\rho): z_{1}<x_{3}<z_{2}\}.$ However, Theorem 4 does not imply any explicit lower bound on the length of $( z_{1},z_{2} )$ or any regularity estimates in such a strip. Theorem B provides a quantitative description of such intervals only in terms of the natural local energies, which will be important for applications in the axially symmetric case (Theorems C and D).

Theorem B (quantitative interval of regularity). Let v be a local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations in $Q (1)$ . For any $0 < \rho < 1$ and any $- 1 < a < b < 1$ there exists an interval $(z_{1}, z_{2}) \subset(a,b)$ , with

$$
\left| z _ {2} - z _ {1} \right| \geq h _ {1} (\mathcal {G}, \mathcal {H}) = (\mathcal {G} + 2) ^ {- M _ {1} \left(\min \{\mathcal {H}, \mathcal {G}\} + 1\right)},
$$

for a constant $M_{1}(\rho,a,b)>0$ , and v is regular in the closure of the domain $\mathcal{I}=\{(x,t)\in$ $Q(\rho):z_{1}<x_{3}<z_{2}\}$ and satisfies the estimates

$$
\left\| \nabla_ {x} ^ {m} v \right\| _ {L ^ {\infty} \left(\overline {{\mathcal {I}}}\right)} \lesssim_ {m} h _ {1} ^ {- (m + 1)}, \quad \forall m = 0, 1, 2, \dots .
$$

(1.16)

8. With simple modifications in the geometries of the proof, we can also obtain the existence of quantitative annulus of regularity. Precisely, for any $0 < \rho <1$ and $0< a < b < 1$ , there exists an interval $( r_{1}, r_{2}) \subset(a,b)$ with

$$
\left| r _ {2} - r _ {1} \right| \geq \widetilde {h _ {1}} (\mathcal {G}, \mathcal {H}) = (\mathcal {G} + 2) ^ {- \widetilde {M _ {1}} (\min \{\mathcal {H}, \mathcal {G} \} + 1)}
$$

where $\widetilde{M}_{1}=\widetilde{M}_{1} (\rho,a,b)>0$ , such that v is regular in the closure of the domain $\widetilde{\mathcal{I}}=$ {(x,t): $r_{1}<|x|<r_{2},-\rho^{2}<t<0$ } , with estimates similar to (1.16).

For comparison and also for applications in the axially symmetric case, we present a similar result concerning the existence of regular epochs (intervals in the time direction), which is less surprising and much easier to prove. Theorem 4 implies that the $\frac{1}{2}$ D Hausdorff measure of the set $\pi_{0}(\mathcal{S}[v])=\{-1<t\leq 0:\left(\mathbb{R}^{3}\times \{t\}\right)\cap \mathcal{S}[v]\neq \emptyset}$ is zero, and it turns out one can obtain Proposition 9 without using the pigeonhole principle for the hollowed dissipation energies $\mathcal{E}_{k}。$

Proposition 9 (quantitative epoch of regularity). Let v be a local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equation in Q(1). For any $0<r<1$ and $-1<a,b<0$ , there exists an interval $(t_{1},t_{2})\subset(a,b)$ with

$$
\left| t _ {2} - t _ {1} \right| \geq h _ {2} (\mathcal {G}) = M _ {2} \left(\mathcal {G} + 1\right) ^ {- M _ {3}},
$$

for a constant $M_{2} ( r,a,b ) > 0$ and an absolute constant $M_{3}>0$ , and v is regular in the closure of the domain $\mathcal{J}=\{(x,t)\in Q(r):t_{1}< t < t_{2}\}$ and satisfies the estimates

$$
\left\| \nabla_ {x} ^ {m} v \right\| _ {L ^ {\infty} (\overline {{\mathcal {J}}})} \lesssim_ {m} h _ {2} ^ {- (m + 1)}, \quad \forall m = 0, 1, 2, \dots .
$$

(1.17)

We mention the recent interesting work of Tao [34], where a quantitative triple-exponential improvement of the $L_{t}^{\infty} L_{x}^{3}$ regularity criterion is proved. The idea is to replace the compactness arguments and unique continuation methods in [20] by suitable quantitative counterparts. See also the works [2, 23, 1] for further developments in this direction. Note that certain quantitative annuli and epochs of regularity are proved for $L_{t}^{\infty} L_{x}^{3}$ global-in-space solutions, and played important roles in [34].

## 1.1.2 Applications in the axially symmetric case

In cylindrical coordinates $(\varrho, \theta,z)$ , we have the orthonormal frame

## 1.1.2 Applications in the axially symmetric case

In cylindrical coordinates $(\varrho, \theta,z)$ , we have the orthonormal frame

$$
e _ {\varrho} = \left( \begin{array}{c} \cos \theta \\ \sin \theta \\ 0 \end{array} \right), \quad e _ {\theta} = \left( \begin{array}{c} - \sin \theta \\ \cos \theta \\ 0 \end{array} \right), \quad e _ {z} = \left( \begin{array}{c} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array} \right),
$$

(1.18)

under which we can write $v=v^{\varrho}e_{\varrho}+v^{\theta}e_{\theta}+v^{z}e_{z}.$ We say that $( v,p )$ is axially symmetric, if the functions $v^{\varrho},v^{\theta},v^{z}, p$ are independent of $\theta\in[0,2\pi).$ An important feature of the axially symmetric Navier-Stokes equations (ASNS) is that the scalar function $\Gamma=\varrho v^{\theta}$ satisfies the transport-diffusion equation

$$
\partial_ {t} \Gamma - \Delta \Gamma + \frac {2}{\varrho} \partial_ {\varrho} \Gamma + b \cdot \nabla \Gamma = 0
$$

(1.19)

where $b=v^{\varrho} e_{\varrho}+v^{z} e_{z}$ . The maximum principle for (1.19) gives the scale-invariant a priori bound for mild solutions to the Cauchy problem:

$$
\left\| \Gamma (t) \right\| _ {L ^ {\infty} \left(\mathbb {R} ^ {3}\right)} \leq \left\| \Gamma (0) \right\| _ {L ^ {\infty} \left(\mathbb {R} ^ {3}\right)}.
$$

(1.20)

Also, by the technique of Moser iteration, $\Gamma$ is locally bounded for any axially symmetric suitable weak solution [29].

(1.20)

Also, by the technique of Moser iteration, $\Gamma$ is locally bounded for any axially symmetric suitable weak solution [29].

In [18], the first author together with Zhang proved global regularity for mild solutions under the assumption that $\Gamma$ enjoys a rather weak modulus of continuity $|\Gamma| \leq C_{*}|\ln \varrho|^{-2}$ near the z-axis. The proof indicates that the global regularity of ASNS is of a critical nature. In [36], Wei weakened the continuity assumption to $|\Gamma| \leq|\ln \varrho|^{-\frac{3}{2}}.$ Moreover, in [18, 36], for the Cauchy problem it is shown that when $\| \Gamma\|_{L^{\infty}}$ is small respect to the initial data, the mild solution stays regular for all times. However, we emphasize that the latter small-swirl regularity results rely heavily on the global-in-space energy estimates for the unknowns $(J,\Omega)=\left(\frac{\omega^{\varrho}} {\varrho},\frac{\omega^{\theta}} {\varrho}\right)$ where $\omega=\omega^{\varrho}e_{\varrho}+\omega^{\theta}e_{\theta}+\omega^{z}e_{z}$ is the vorticity, which do not allow the use of cut-off functions in the z-direction. See also [21] for a related study for critical initial data.

In Section 5, as an application of Theorem B, we prove a quantitative local small-swirl regularity criterion for ASNS. Note that it is not so difficult to prove a non-quantitative version (see Proposition 17) based on contradiction and compactness arguments. However, the quantification of the proof is a nontrivial task. Using Theorem B, we resolve the difficulties in localizing the energy estimates for $( J,\Omega)$ and thus obtain:

Theorem C (local small-swirl regularity). Let v be an axially symmetric local suitable weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equation in $Q (1)$ . There exists an absolute constant $M_{4}>0$ such that, if

$$
\| \Gamma \| _ {L ^ {\infty} (Q (1))} \leq M _ {4} ^ {- 1} \left[ \left(\min \{\mathcal {H}, \mathcal {G} \} + 1\right) \ln (\mathcal {G} + 2) \right] ^ {- \frac {3}{2}},
$$

(1.21)

then v is regular in $Q(\frac{1}{2})$

It is desirable to replace the condition (1.21) by an absolute smallness assumption $\| \Gamma\|_{L^{\infty}(Q(1))}\leq c$ , where c is independent of $v^{\varrho}$ and $v^{z}.$ To the best of our knowledge, this is beyond the reach of existing methods.

An interesting application of Theorem C is a slightly supercritical improvement of the CKN criterion for ASNS. Although we have improved partial regularity for the general Navier-Stokes equations, we can only improve the CKN criterion in the axially symmetric case. In the important works [16, 5, 4], regularity of ASNS is proved under the pointwise Type I bound

$$
| v | \leq \frac {C _ {*}}{\varrho^ {\alpha} \sqrt {- t} ^ {1 - \alpha}}, \quad \alpha \in [ 0, 1 ].
$$

(1.22)

In [29], the one-point Type I result for suitable weak solutions to ASNS

$$
\limsup _ {r \rightarrow 0 +} \frac {1}{r} \int_ {Q (r)} | \nabla v | ^ {2} d x d t < + \infty \Longrightarrow (0, 0) \notin \mathcal {S} [ v ].
$$

(1.23)

(1.23)

is established via compactness arguments and Liouville theorem. There are a few slightly supercritical generalizations of the Type I results. A slight improvement of (1.22), $\alpha=0$ case, is given by Pan [24]. By the more recent works [7,31] (and Lemma 12), regularity of a local suitable weak solution can be proved if, for a small $\nu>0$

$$
\sup _ {w \in Q (1)} \limsup _ {r \rightarrow 0 +} \frac {\int_ {Q (r , w)} | \nabla v | ^ {2} d x d t}{r (\ln | \ln r |) ^ {\nu}} < + \infty .
$$

(1.24)

Our next result is a corollary of Theorem C, from which all the (slightly supercritical) Type I results in the literature can be deduced (see Remark 20 for details).

Theorem D (Improved CKN criterion). There exists an absolute constant $\mu>0$ such that, for any axially symmetric local suitable weak solution $v$ to the Navier-Stokes equations in $Q (1)$

$$
\limsup _ {r \rightarrow 0 +} \frac {\int_ {Q (r)} | \nabla v | ^ {2} d x d t}{r (\ln | \ln r |) ^ {\mu}} < + \infty \Rightarrow (0, 0) \notin S [ v ].
$$

(1.25)

Theorem D directly improves Seregin's one-point result (1.23). Our condition (1.25) is much weaker than (1.24) since the bound is assumed only at a single point. We emphasize that a direct consequence of Theorem D or (1.24) reads: there exist $\kappa,\sigma>0$ such that for all $0\leq\alpha\leq1$ , we have

$$
| v | \leq C _ {*} \frac {\left(\ln | \ln \varrho |\right) ^ {\kappa} \cdot \left(\ln | \ln (- t) |\right) ^ {\sigma}}{\varrho^ {\alpha} \sqrt {- t} ^ {1 - \alpha}} \mathrm {i n} Q (r) \mathrm {f o r s o m e} r > 0 \Longrightarrow (0, 0) \notin S [ v ].
$$

This obviously improves the Type I criteria in [16, 5, 4] and generalizes the result of [24].

Finally, we point out that via standard covering arguments, Theorem D implies the partial regularity result $\mathcal{P}^{f}(\mathcal{S}[v])=0$ for $f=r(\ln|\ln r|)^{\mu}$ , a statement weaker than Theorem A. It is an interesting question whether (1.25) still holds true with $(\ln|\ln r|)^{\mu}$ in the denominator replaced by $|\ln r|.$ We also mention that the recent numerical results [13] seem to suggest that ASNS may develop singularity in a nearly self-similar scenario where the blow-up rate is Type I with some logarithmic corrections.

## 1.2 Organization

In Section 2, we introduce the notations to be used throughout the paper, and state a few preliminary lemmas on scale-invariant quantities and coverings. In Section 3, we use a quantitative version of the CKN criterion and the pigeonhole principle to prove Theorem A. In Section 4, we prove the quantitative results concerning the intervals and epochs of regularity, i.e., Theorem B and Proposition 9. In Section 5, for comparison, we first prove a non-quantitative version of Theorem C using a compactness argument. Then we apply the results of Section 4 to show Theorem C. Theorem D is finally deduced as a corollary of Theorem C. The proofs of the auxiliary Lemmas 18 & 19 are given in the Appendix.

## 2.3 Covering lemmas

We recall the following version of Vitali covering lemma for parabolic cylinders, see, e.g., [3], Lemma 6.1].

Lemma 13. Let $\mathfrak{I}$ be any collection of parabolic cylinders $\{Q^{+}(r,w)\}$ contained in a bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}_{x}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}_{t}$ .
